description: Na₆CaZr(SiO₃)₆ crystallizes in the trigonal R3c space group. There are two inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to two equivalent O atoms. There is one shorter (2.27 Å) and one longer (2.28 Å) Na-O bond length. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 7-coordinate geometry to seven O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.27-2.90 Å. Ca is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted CaO₆ octahedra that share corners with six equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra and  a faceface with one ZrO₆ octahedra. There are three shorter (2.28 Å) and three longer (2.57 Å) Ca-O bond lengths. Zr is bonded to six O atoms to form ZrO₆ octahedra that share corners with six SiO₄ tetrahedra and  a faceface with one CaO₆ octahedra. There are three shorter (2.08 Å) and three longer (2.17 Å) Zr-O bond lengths. There are two inequivalent Si sites. In the first Si site, Si is bonded to four O atoms to form SiO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one ZrO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent CaO₆ octahedra, and corners with two equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 38-50°. There are a spread of Si-O bond distances ranging from 1.61-1.67 Å. In the second Si site, Si is bonded to four O atoms to form SiO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one ZrO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 35°. There are a spread of Si-O bond distances ranging from 1.58-1.67 Å. There are six inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded to three Na and one Si atom to form distorted corner-sharing ONa₃Si trigonal pyramids. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na, one Zr, and one Si atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na and two Si atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ca, one Zr, and one Si atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ca, and one Si atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na and two Si atoms.
